does: Cooks food in plenty of fast-bubbling salted water, so that it is done quickly and evenly.

intro.what: Food cooks in a large pot of actively bubbling water.
intro.why: Recognizing the strength of the boil and the food texture helps you manage heat after food enters the pot.

how: Fill a large pot with far more water than the food needs.
Bring it to a rolling boil and salt it until it tastes pleasantly salty.
Add the food and bring the water back to the boil as fast as you can.
Test a piece often, and lift the food out the moment it is tender.

cues.text: Big bubbles that keep rolling even when you stir.
The tip of a knife slides into a vegetable with only slight resistance.

mistakes.mistake: Too little water, so it stops boiling when the food goes in and green vegetables turn dull.
mistakes.fix: Use a bigger pot and more water, and cook in batches.
Salt it well. Food boiled in plain water tastes flat, however it is seasoned later.

quiz.question: Why use ample water in this boiling method?
choices: It prevents any movement between the pieces.
It helps maintain the boil when food is added.
It replaces the need to restore heat after adding food.
quiz.because: A larger volume is less easily cooled by the incoming food.

quiz.question: What should happen after food enters the pot?
choices: Keep the reduced heat without restoring bubbling.
Leave the food resting while the water cools.
Bring the water back to a rolling boil.
quiz.because: Adding food can slow bubbling, so the method calls for restoring the boil.

quiz.question: What does a rolling boil look like?
choices: Large bubbles keep moving even when stirred.
A still surface with occasional tiny bubbles.
A steaming surface with small bubbles only around the edge.
quiz.because: Persistent large bubbles distinguish boiling from gentler heating.

quiz.question: The pot stops boiling and vegetables become dull. What should change?
choices: Pack more vegetables into the same water.
Use a larger pot with more water and avoid crowding.
Keep the heat lower after adding the food.
quiz.because: More water and less crowding help the pot recover its boil.
